predecessors.name: Bahmani Sultanate
predecessors.text: the Bahmani heartland around Bidar, the Bahmani capital since 1429, and the eastern (Telangana) lands that Cliopatria draws inside Bidar to 1518

successors.name: Bijapur Sultanate
successors.text: the whole of Bidar, 'annexed to Bijapur sultanate' after the defeat of Amir Barid III in 1619

ledger.x: 1492: Qasim Barid I takes control of the Bahmani state at Bidar and founds the Barid Shahi line.
1518-1519: the eastern lands pass to the new sultanate of Golconda.
1527: the Bahmani state formally ends at Bidar.
1542: Ali Barid Shah I is the first Barid to take the royal title of Shah, making Bidar a kingdom in name as well as fact.
1619: the Barid Shahi sultanate ends; Bidar is annexed to Bijapur (infobox 'Disestablished: 1619').

wars.name: Battle of Talikota
wars.outcome: Victory of the Deccan sultanates; Rama Raya killed (23 January 1565) and Vijayanagara plundered.

wars.name: Bijapur conquest of Bidar
wars.outcome: Bijapur victory: Amir Barid III is defeated and Bidar is annexed to Bijapur.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary survey or treaty line for Bidar; the frontiers with Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar are Cliopatria's approximations.
